decisions.decision: Add `spec-tables` CI job and verification script comparing implementations to spec tables.
decisions.rationale: Every implementation read the spec only to assert it contained "Deterministic CBOR", while hand-typed test tables were never verified directly against the document's tables.
decisions.quote: Parses the spec's tables rather than quoting them, and compares all four implementations against them in both directions. 38 comparisons, its own CI job.

decisions.decision: Implement BLAKE3-256 and C-Produce UID derivation in `nodejs/`.
decisions.rationale: Testing against a C library binding would test two callers of one implementation rather than proving the spec is sufficient, so BLAKE3 was hand-rolled to provide an independent derivation.
decisions.quote: nodejs/src/blake3.js is a hand-rolled BLAKE3-256, for the reason the other two are: a binding to the same C library the Rust calls would test two callers of one implementation.

decisions.decision: Document normative status integers, source map layout, kind enum, base32 alphabet, and empty set omission in spec.
decisions.rationale: Implementations had previously deduced these normative details only by decoding fixtures rather than reading the spec, and empty deps/grounds were incorrectly documented as required.
decisions.quote: The reading found four facts a C-Produce implementer cannot proceed without, none of them in the document. All four are now at §2.1 and §2.2, and marked SPEC: at the point of use

decisions.decision: Normalize text to NFC in the Node.js CBOR encoder.
decisions.rationale: §3 constraint 6 explicitly mandates normalization at the encoder, which is needed so that authored decomposed Unicode strings match canonical fixture UIDs.
decisions.quote: One behaviour change outside the new files: the CBOR encoder now NFC-normalises text, which §3 constraint 6 asks for by name ("normalise at the encoder").

decisions.decision: Replay tutorial chapters sequentially using scratch workspaces and `edits.json` reader edits.
decisions.rationale: Fixtures were previously keyed by filename instead of position, preventing states printed as fragments or diffs from being replayed safely without mutating committed files.
decisions.quote: verify-doc-output.py now replays a chapter as a chapter: a scratch copy of its fixtures, walked in document order, with fmt --write allowed to write.

decisions.decision: Hold back repair of chapter 29's `beta.smy` drift.
decisions.rationale: The missing stanza cannot be deduced or reconstructed directly from the printed chapter, so guessing what it was is unacceptable.
decisions.quote: Held back rather than repaired: the missing stanza cannot be reconstructed from the page, and guessing one into a published chapter is not a repair.

decisions.decision: Decline implementing rule M in outside reader implementations.
decisions.rationale: Rule M constrains unit status against grounds statuses which are held in a store rather than in unit cores, so validating it on a unit alone cannot fail without building a store.
decisions.quote: Rule M is implemented by none of the three outside readers, deliberately. It constrains a unit against the statuses of its grounds, and a unit core carries grounds as uids — so M is checkable against a store and not against a unit

decisions.decision: Fix incorrect spec section citations in Go and Python UID implementations.
decisions.rationale: The implementations cited nonexistent sections (§1.1), which reads misleadingly as a settled clause.
decisions.quote: go/uid.go, python/smysl/uid.py and nodejs/src/uid.js each cited a section the format spec has never had.

prerequisites.text: Node.js does not provide a BLAKE3 implementation in its standard library.
prerequisites.quote: Node has no BLAKE3 in its standard library

prerequisites.text: The CBOR decoder already rejects any input text that is not NFC-normalized.
prerequisites.quote: the decoder rejects anything not already NFC

prerequisites.text: Unit cores store grounds solely as UIDs without retaining their corresponding status values.
prerequisites.quote: a unit core carries its grounds as uids — the statuses they name are not in hand.

prerequisites.text: Section 1 of the format specification contains no subsections.
prerequisites.quote: There is no §1.1 — §1 has no subsections.

alternatives.alternative: Quoting the spec's tables in hand-typed test assertions.
alternatives.reason: Editing the spec and editing tests would remain separate acts unable to catch mismatches.
alternatives.quote: Parses the spec's tables rather than quoting them

alternatives.alternative: Using a binding to the same C library that Rust calls.
alternatives.reason: It would test two callers of one implementation rather than proving the specification is sufficient.
alternatives.quote: a binding to the same C library the Rust calls would test two callers of one implementation

alternatives.alternative: Splitting multi-state tutorial files into separate files for each step.
alternatives.reason: It would force the chapters to name different files at each step, changing what the book teaches.
alternatives.quote: Splitting them would mean the chapters naming a different file at each step, which changes what they teach.

alternatives.alternative: Repairing chapter 29's beta.smy immediately by guessing the missing stanza.
alternatives.reason: The missing stanza cannot be reconstructed from the page and guessing is not an acceptable repair.
alternatives.quote: Held back rather than repaired: the missing stanza cannot be reconstructed from the page, and guessing one into a published chapter is not a repair.

alternatives.alternative: Enforcing Rule M directly in outside reader unit validation.
alternatives.reason: Rule M requires inspecting grounds statuses stored elsewhere, so a unit-level check cannot fail.
alternatives.quote: a `validate` claiming to enforce it would be a check that cannot fail.

consequences.text: Uncovers masthead version drift and phantom section citations across implementations.
consequences.quote: It found four more on its first run: the masthead read `smysl/0.1` while §8.6 of the same document says `smysl/1.0` is what new documents declare; and go/uid.go, python/smysl/uid.py and nodejs/src/uid.js each cited a section the format spec has never had.
consequences.verification_quote: Eight breakages verified, each failing the right check: a status row deleted from the spec, a unit-core key renumbered, an undocumented status added to an implementation, a record code renumbered, a record renamed, a source key shifted, the masthead reverted, and a phantom citation reintroduced.

consequences.text: Node.js reproduces all canonical wire encodings and expands test coverage to 126 tests.
consequences.quote: `nodejs/src/uid.js` reproduces all sixteen canonical encodings and all sixteen uids in `fixtures/wire/uid/cases.json`, and implements §7's *shape* clause with `uid()` running it first — a malformed unit cannot obtain an identity from the package, which is what makes the class a claim about emitting.
consequences.verification_quote: Eight new invariants, each verified capable of failing before being trusted: status dropped from the hashed core, NFC removed from the encoder, empty sets emitted, the source keys shifted, the sort dropped, base32hex substituted, `validate` ungated from `uid()`, and the BLAKE3 tree ignored. Eight breakages, eight distinct failures, each naming its clause.

consequences.text: Enables reproducing the decomposed Unicode fixture in Node.js UID calculations.
consequences.quote: It was a no-op for C-Read — the decoder rejects anything not already NFC — and is what makes `unicode-decomposed` reproducible.
consequences.verification_quote: Eight new invariants, each verified capable of failing before being trusted: status dropped from the hashed core, NFC removed from the encoder, empty sets emitted, the source keys shifted, the sort dropped, base32hex substituted, `validate` ungated from `uid()`, and the BLAKE3 tree ignored. Eight breakages, eight distinct failures, each naming its clause.

consequences.text: Replays 85 transcripts end-to-end while surfacing real transcript drift in chapter 29.
consequences.quote: 78 → 85 replayed, with `first.smy`'s whole four-state narrative now running end to end, and `step1 → step2 → step3` in chapter 4 — one document under three names, none of the later two committable.
consequences.verification_quote: Three breakages verified: an anchor that stops resolving, a stanza match that finds nothing, and a base fixture edited away from its chapter.

consequences.text: Leaves seven transcripts blocked from replay until the missing chapter stanza is known.
consequences.quote: Restoring it makes seven more commands replayable at once, the largest single block left.

consequences.text: Avoids introducing a validation check that cannot fail without a full store.
consequences.quote: M is checkable against a store and not against a unit, so a `validate` claiming to enforce it would be a check that cannot fail.

consequences.text: Prevents misleading readers with citations to nonexistent specification sections.
consequences.quote: A citation to a section that does not exist reads as a clause settling the question
consequences.verification_quote: Eight breakages verified, each failing the right check: a status row deleted from the spec, a unit-core key renumbered, an undocumented status added to an implementation, a record code renumbered, a record renamed, a source key shifted, the masthead reverted, and a phantom citation reintroduced.
